chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Halabi and Fadalah from Aban from Muhammad Al-Halabi and Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Whatever food, goods, or things differ in quality such that one is superior to the other, there is no harm in selling it, two of the inferior kind for one of the superior kind, hand to hand; but as for deferment (delay in delivery), it is not valid."

key_terms.مِثْلَيْنِ بِمِثْلٍ: two of one kind for one of another kind (referring to unequal exchange)
key_terms.يَتَفَاضَلُ: to differ in quality or superiority

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling unequal quantities of different quality goods in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the permissibility of 'fadl' (excess in quantity/quality) in barter transactions, distinguishing it from 'riba al-fadl' by requiring immediate, hand-to-hand exchange. It establishes that while unequal quantities are allowed for non-staple goods, any delay in delivery invalidates the trade, a principle central to Shia commercial jurisprudence.
